title: Find the Lexicographically Largest String From the Box II
statement:
Alice runs a game for her `numFriends` friends using the string `word`. Each round cuts `word` into exactly `numFriends` non-empty consecutive pieces, no two rounds cut it the same way, and the game goes on until every possible way of cutting has been used. After each round, all of that round's pieces are dropped into a box. Return the lexicographically largest string in the box when the game is over.

Strings compare letter by letter: at the first position where two strings differ, the one whose letter comes later in the alphabet is larger. When one string is a prefix of the other, the longer one is larger.
constraints: word consists only of lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Each piece leaves `numFriends - 1` others that need a letter each, so a piece has at most `m = n - numFriends + 1` letters. With `numFriends >= 2`, a piece starting at any index `i` can take all `min(m, n - i)` letters, because the letters around it can always form the other pieces. A string beats its own prefixes, so the best piece starting at `i` is `word.slice(i, i + m)`. Cutting two suffixes to `m` letters never reverses their order, so the best of these is the largest suffix of `word`, cut to `m` letters. With `numFriends = 1` the only piece is `word`.

Trying every substring takes O(n³), and even comparing all suffixes is O(n²) on words like `"zzz...z"`. Two pointers find the largest suffix in O(n).

## Approach

1. If `numFriends` is `1`, return `word`.
2. `i` is the best suffix start so far and `j` a challenger; compare them letter by letter at offset `k`.
3. Equal letters: `k++`.
4. `word[i + k]` is bigger: the challenger loses, and so does each start from `j + 1` to `j + k` (beaten by the matching start after `i`). Set `j = j + k + 1`, `k = 0`.
5. `word[j + k]` is bigger: likewise the starts `i` to `i + k` lose. Set `i = max(i + k + 1, j)`, `j = i + 1`, `k = 0`.
6. Once `j + k` reaches `n`, `i` starts the largest suffix: return `word.slice(i, i + n - numFriends + 1)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "dbca"`, `numFriends = 2`, `n = 4`; start with `i = 0`, `j = 1`, `k = 0`. `'d'` beats `'b'`, so `j = 2`; it beats `'c'`, so `j = 3`; it beats `'a'`, so `j = 4` and the loop ends. The largest suffix is `"dbca"`, and a piece holds at most `4 - 2 + 1 = 3` letters, so the answer is `"dbc"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each round raises `i + j + k`, which stays below `2n`.
- Space: O(1) apart from the returned string.

## Pitfalls

- With `numFriends = 1` the box holds only `word`, even when a later suffix is larger: `"ab"` gives `"ab"`, not `"b"` (Test 2).
- Take the longest allowed piece: `"dbca"` gives `"dbc"`, not `"d"`.
- The first copy of the biggest letter is not always the right start: in `"zzazzb"` (Test 7) the answer `"zzb"` starts at index 3.
- When the challenger wins, move `i` past `i + k`, not just to `j`; otherwise words like `"aaa...ab"` take quadratic time.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `word` |
| `i` | start of the largest suffix found so far |
| `j` | start of the suffix challenging it |
| `k` | number of letters the two suffixes are known to share |

narration.2: With one friend the only piece is the whole word.
narration.5: i is the start of the best suffix found so far.
narration.6: j is the start of the suffix challenging it.
narration.7: k counts the letters the two suffixes are known to share.
narration.8: Keep comparing while the challenger still has a letter at offset k.
narration.9: Same letter at offset k: the comparison is not decided yet.
narration.11: The best suffix has the bigger letter, so the challenger loses.
narration.12: Each start from j + 1 to j + k is beaten by the matching start after i, so skip them all.
narration.13: Compare the new challenger from its first letter.
narration.15: The challenger wins: the starts i to i + k all lose, so the best start moves to j or beyond.
narration.16: The next challenger starts right after the new best start.
narration.17: Compare from the first letter again.
narration.21: Cut the largest suffix to the longest piece allowed, n - numFriends + 1 letters.
